subject: history_social
passage: In the 1700s and early 1800s, stagecoaches carried passengers and mail along the main roads of Britain. A team of horses could not gallop for long without tiring, so the roads were lined with coaching inns about every fifteen kilometers. At each inn, workers led the tired horses away and hitched a fresh team to the coach, often in only a few minutes. Passengers barely had time to stretch their legs before the coach rolled on.
stem: According to the text, what happened at coaching inns?

choices.A: Passengers stayed overnight while their horses rested.
choices.B: Mail was sorted and handed over to local carriers.
choices.C: Tired horses were replaced with a fresh team.
choices.D: Coaches were repaired before continuing along the road.

explanation.why: The question asks for what the text says happened at the inns. The third sentence states it directly: "workers led the tired horses away and hitched a fresh team to the coach, often in only a few minutes."
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text says passengers "barely had time to stretch their legs" before moving on, so they did not stay overnight.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text says coaches carried mail but never describes sorting or handing it over at inns.
explanation.C: Correct. This restates the text's description of workers swapping the tired horses for a fresh team.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text does not mention repairs to the coaches.
